name: qlrisk_simulate_paths
title: Monte Carlo path generation
description: Simulate stochastic-process paths with qlrisk's Monte Carlo library: gbm, ou, cir, heston, vasicek, hull_white, merton_jump. Rate models (ou, cir, vasicek, hull_white) use initial_value as the starting rate and mean_reversion_speed / long_term_mean; heston adds vol_of_vol, correlation, initial_variance; merton_jump adds jump_intensity, jump_mean, jump_std. Returns summary statistics on up to 60 time points, the terminal distribution and a few sample paths (not the full path matrix). Inputs: process, initial_value, drift, volatility, maturity, num_paths; the rest (num_steps, mean_reversion_speed, long_term_mean, vol_of_vol, correlation, initial_variance, jump_intensity, jump_mean, jump_std, seed, percentiles, sample_paths) in the optional `advanced` object. Inputs: process, initial_value, drift, volatility, maturity, num_paths; the rest (num_steps, mean_reversion_speed, long_term_mean, vol_of_vol, correlation, initial_variance, jump_intensity, jump_mean, jump_std, seed, percentiles, sample_paths) in the optional `advanced` object. Example: {"process": "gbm", "initial_value": 100, "drift": 0.05, "volatility": 0.2, "maturity": 1, "num_paths": 10000} gives 10000 gbm paths x 252 steps: terminal mean 105.157, std 21.382.
